title: Stein factorization of a proper algebraic space over an affine scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $f:X\to T$ a proper morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Put $B=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$, the ring of global sections of its small etale structure sheaf, and let $A\to B$ be pullback by $f$. Evaluation of global functions defines a morphism $q:X\to Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $f=\pi q$ for $\pi:Z\to T$ induced by $A\to B$. The map $\pi$ is integral, meaning that each element of $B$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The map $q$ is proper. For every field $K$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$, the fibre $X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}K$ is nonempty and geometrically connected: after every field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension] its point space is nonempty and has no partition into two nonempty relatively open subsets. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. No Noetherian, flatness, finite-presentation, reducedness, or scheme-representability hypothesis on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A1C, theorem-stein-factorization-general, clauses (1), (2), (4), over an affine scheme target; canonical evaluation and surjectivity are also in Tag 0A19, lemma-stein-universally-closed.

proof.text: Apply the affine-target global-functions bijection to $X$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with the ring map $B\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ equal to the identity. This constructs the evaluation morphism $q$. The morphism $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(A\to B)$ exists by the spectrum construction. The pullbacks of $f$ and $\pi q$ on global functions are both the specified $A\to B$, so injectivity of the same bijection for target $T$ gives $f=\pi q$. In particular $q^\sharp:B\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=B$ is the identity, not merely an unspecified ring isomorphism.

The scheme morphism $\pi$ has affine source $Z$, so it is separated by the affine-source separatedness theorem. This is also separatedness as a morphism of algebraic spaces, since the scheme diagonal and its scheme tests are the same diagonal. Proper cancellation, applied to $X\xrightarrow q Z\xrightarrow\pi T$ and the given proper composite $f$, now proves that $q$ is proper. In particular $q$ is quasi-compact. Its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence proper and quasi-compact by the closed-immersion theorem, so $q$ is quasi-separated as required for flat cohomology base change below.

source.place: Tag 04NX, lemma-universally-closed-permanence, (2); scheme separatedness from Schemes Tags 01KN and 01KV.

proof.text: The affine qcqs theorem makes $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply proper Noetherian approximation to obtain a small nonempty directed system $X_i\to T_i$ of proper finitely presented morphisms, affine transitions on both systems, and limit $X\to T$. Each $T_i$ is finitely presented over $\mathbf Z$, and both $T_i$ and $X_i$ are qcqs. Since $T$ is affine, the affine-limit theorem makes all $T_i$ affine after restricting to a final tail (cofinal since directedness gives a common upper bound with its initial index). Write $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ there. Each $T_i$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ (forget the finite relations in its local finite presentations), hence Noetherian by finite-type inheritance. Applying the affine-open theorem to the whole affine open $T_i\subset T_i$ shows that $A_i$ is a Noetherian ring.

source.place: Tag 0A0X, lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian; Tag 07SQ, lemma-limit-is-affine; scheme Noetherian inheritance Tag 01T6.

proof.text: For every remaining $i$, properness makes $X_i\to T_i$ quasi-separated and of finite type, so $X_i$ is Noetherian by the coherent-Noetherian theorem. Its structure module $\mathcal O_{X_i}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (locally free of rank one), hence coherent by that theorem. Apply proper coherent Ext finiteness with $E=F=\mathcal O_{X_i}[0]$ and $n=0$. Both boundedness hypotheses hold because these complexes have cohomology only in degree zero. The single-complex embedding is fully faithful, so the resulting finite $A_i$-module is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X_i}}(\mathcal O_{X_i},\mathcal O_{X_i})$. Evaluation at $1$ identifies this with $B_i=\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal O_{X_i})$: its inverse sends a section $b$ to multiplication by its restrictions on every site object. These maps respect the $A_i$-action induced by $X_i\to T_i$. Thus $B_i$ is a finite $A_i$-module.

source.place: Tag 0D0T, lemma-ext-finite, specialized to two structure modules in degree zero; derived.tex Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts (2).

proof.text: The global-sections limit theorem, applied to the two qcqs systems with affine transitions, identifies $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ and $B=\varinjlim_i B_i$, compatibly with the structure ring maps. Let $b\in B$. It is the pullback of some $b_i\in B_i$. Finiteness from the preceding step and finite-algebra integrality give $b_i^n+a_{n-1}b_i^{n-1}+\cdots+a_0=0$, with $a_j\in A_i$ and leading coefficient $1$. Pulling this equality to $B$ yields exactly the same monic equation for $b$, with each coefficient mapped along $A_i\to A\to B$. Every $b$ is therefore integral over $A$, which is the asserted integrality of $\pi$. This argument asserts finiteness only at the Noetherian stages, not finiteness of $B$ over the original $A$.

Fix a prime $z\subset B$ and put $R=B_z$, with residue field $k=\kappa(z)$. A separable closure $k^s/k$ exists by the separable-closure theorem. Form the strict henselization $H=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ using the triples theorem: $H$ is local and henselian, and its residue field is the chosen $k^s$. The map $R\to H$ is faithfully flat. The localization $B\to R$ is flat, and composition of flat ring maps shows that $B\to H$ is flat. The affine flatness equivalence makes $\operatorname{Spec}H\to Z$ flat as a scheme morphism. Put $Y=X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}H$ and $Y_0=Y\times_H\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. Proper base change makes both $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ and $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ proper. Under the specified residue map, $Y_0$ is $X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ over $z$.

source.place: Tags 04GP and 04GW, strict henselization; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM (1), faithfully flat; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04WP, proper base change.

proof.text: Apply degree-zero flat cohomology base change to $q$, the flat map $\operatorname{Spec}H\to Z$, and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal O_X$. Tensor pullback of the structure module is the structure module. Since $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=B$ as a $B$-module via the identity $q^\sharp$ established in step 1, the base-change isomorphism gives $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=B\otimes_BH=H$. This is an isomorphism of rings over $H$: the canonical map sends $b\otimes h$ to the product of the pulled-back section $b$ and the structural section $h$, and hence preserves multiplication and the unit. Thus the structural map $H\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is itself an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 073K, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, q=0 on affine targets.

proof.text: The local ring $H$ is nonzero. If $|Y|$ were empty, every scheme atlas would be empty and the sheaf axiom for the empty covering would give $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0$, contradicting the preceding isomorphism with $H$. Thus $Y$ is nonempty. Clopen subsets of $|Y|$ correspond to idempotents of $H$ by the global-idempotent theorem. A local ring has only the idempotents $0,1$, and their corresponding subspaces are respectively $\varnothing,Y$. Hence $Y$ admits no nontrivial clopen subset and is connected.

source.place: Tag 03BZ, lemma-open-subspaces, and the idempotent/decomposition argument in spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 0DMY; local idempotents as in algebra.tex Tag 00E9.

proof.text: The image of the nonempty $|Y|$ in $\operatorname{Spec}H$ is a nonempty closed subset, by properness. Any prime of a local ring is contained in its maximal ideal, so its closure contains the closed point; consequently this image contains the closed point. The point-space fibre-product surjectivity theorem then gives a point of $Y_0$. Thus $Y_0$ is nonempty. This uses closedness, not a claim that a nonempty space over a local base always has a nonempty closed fibre.

source.place: Tag 04WP, lemma-base-change-proper, and the definition of universally closed; spaces-properties point-space fibre-product calculus.

proof.text: Suppose $|Y_0|$ has a nontrivial clopen subset. The clopen-subspace correspondence supplies its open-subspace structure $U\subset Y_0$. Its inclusion is a closed immersion: on any scheme test the preimage is clopen, and it is cut out by the ideal sheaf which is zero on that open and the unit ideal on its open complement. The closed-immersion theorem and proper composition therefore make $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ proper. Since $H$ is henselian local, $(H,\mathfrak m_H)$ is a henselian pair. Apply proper clopen lifting to the separated finite-type $H$-space $Y$ and this $U$: it gives a clopen $W\subset Y$ with $W_0=U$. Connectedness of $Y$ forces $W=\varnothing$ or $Y$, so $U=\varnothing$ or $Y_0$, a contradiction. Together with step 9 this proves $Y_0$ connected.

source.place: Tag 0CWI, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, with I the maximal ideal; properness permanence Tags 04XZ and 04XY.

proof.text: Because $k^s$ is separably closed, the separably-closed components theorem makes the nonempty connected $Y_0$ geometrically connected: $Y_0\times_{k^s}E$ is nonempty connected for every extension $E/k^s$. Now take any $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ and any extension $L/K$. Its image is a prime $z$ and the ring map factors through $k=\kappa(z)$: elements outside $z$ become invertible, and $zB_z$ maps to zero. Apply the preceding construction at this $z$. The common-extension theorem gives a field $E$ containing compatible copies of $k^s$ and $L$ over $k$. The space $Y_0\times_{k^s}E=X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}E$ is nonempty connected. Its projection to $X\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}L$ is continuous and surjective: $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is surjective, and the point-space fibre-product theorem preserves that surjectivity on this pullback. A continuous surjective image of a nonempty connected space is nonempty connected (a putative clopen partition pulls back to such a partition). This proves the required assertion for every $K$ and $L/K$. If $B$ is the zero ring there are no field-valued points of $Z$, so the fibre assertion is vacuous and the preceding construction and integrality proof still apply.
